title: Microsoft Teams: AI-powered insights on meeting quality in the Teams admin center
summary: The briefing agrees with the roadmap and Microsoft's tenant notice, including the rollout windows, administrator roles and excluded telemetry. The cited control references now open successfully. Minor corrections should acknowledge the general Teams licence requirement and complete the role-assignment guidance.

claims.quote: This feature uses AI/machine learning to analyze historical meeting-quality data and surface insights to admins; it does not alter how customer data is stored or processed.

claims.claim: Existing troubleshooting obfuscates identifiable information for federated and external participants.
claims.quote: For federated and external participants, end-user identifiable information (EUII) is obfuscated to protect privacy in accordance with Microsoft data handling policies.

claims.claim: Existing troubleshooting does not obfuscate relevant identifiable information in peer-to-peer calls.
claims.quote: For peer-to-peer (P2P) calls, relevant EUII is **not** obfuscated because the shared call session requires participant information to support effective troubleshooting.

claims.quote: Searched: "meeting quality" "insights" "external" obfuscated. Opened monitor-troubleshoot-teams-meetings-calls; its obfuscation text covers existing participant troubleshooting, not the new location/public-IP insights.

claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence specific to these insights has been published.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included under the standard's product-level licensing rule. Replace the opening licensing sentence with: 'Teams requires a Teams license except for joining meetings anonymously; no licence specific to these insights is yet published.' Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/user-access to sources and retain the warning not to assume the existing telemetry entitlements apply to the insights. This does not assert that a feature-specific add-on has been ruled out.

claims.claim: Role assignment starts at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > Users > select the user > Assigned roles > Add assignments.
claims.quote: Browse to **Entra ID** > **Users**. Search for and select the user getting the role assignment. Select **Assigned roles** from the side menu, then select **Add assignments**.
claims.fix: The printed steps are correct but stop at the entry to the assignment flow. Extend controls[1].ui.path and its table rendering to 'Entra ID > Users > select the user > Assigned roles > Add assignments > select a role > Assignment type', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/fundamentals/users-assign-role-azure-portal.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments creates a Microsoft Entra directory role assignment.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Keep the call unchanged. Add to controls[1].note and its rendered note: 'The request body uses principalId for the assignee, roleDefinitionId for the role and directoryScopeId for the directory scope.' These properties are documented in the cited reference.
